 Learn more VEON reported third quarter 2026 sales of US$1,307 million with net income of US$188 million, a shift from a loss a year earlier, and raised full year revenue growth guidance to a range of 16% to 18%. 
 The return to quarterly profitability, alongside a slightly higher revenue growth floor, signals improving operational execution and cost control across VEON's portfolio. 
 We will now see how VEON's return to quarterly profitability might reshape the existing investment narrative built around its digital ecosystem. 
 Scan VEON's guidance reset alongside a wider field and compare it with other high-execution stories using the 35 high quality undervalued stocks that pass strict quality and valuation filters. 
 VEON Investment Narrative Recap 
 For VEON, the big picture is simple. You need to believe the telecom backbone can keep funding a higher margin digital ecosystem across Pakistan, Ukraine, Bangladesh, Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan, while inflation, energy costs and tax changes stay manageable. The analyst consensus Narrative on Simply Wall St leans on digital services already carrying solid EBITDA margins and on fintech like JazzCash and Bangladesh's Mukto Pay to support earnings power. 
 The latest quarter back in profit and a small lift to revenue growth guidance to 16% to 18% give more credibility to that execution story in the near term. The key short term catalyst remains delivery on digital monetisation and cost efficiency. The biggest risk still sits with macro pressure on customer spending and returns from large committed investments in Pakistan and Central Asia. 
 The most relevant piece of news here is the raised 2026 revenue growth guidance from 15% to a range of 16% to 18%. That update lands alongside quarterly sales of US$1,307 million and net income of US$188 million, which marks a return to profit compared with the prior year period's loss. It points to better alignment between VEON's growth ambitions and its current operational run rate. 
 For you as a shareholder, that guidance tweak matters because the core catalysts are execution in digital services and capital discipline, including the plan to keep leverage around 1.1x and convert equity free cash flow into recurring returns. If inflation, energy costs or tax changes bite harder, or if the US$1.5b Pakistan program and roughly US$100m Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan technology agreement fail to deliver adequate returns, the raised growth band could prove hard to sustain. 
 VEON's current earnings of $59.0 million sit against analyst expectations for $798.9 million of earnings and $6.4b of revenue by 2029. This implies 10.3% yearly revenue growth and an earnings increase of about $740 million by that year.

 One bullish twist in the alternate VEON story is Bangladesh. The most optimistic analysts were already banking on digital banking and Mukto Pay helping push revenue toward about US$6.7b and earnings near US$907.8 million by 2029. Those projections came before this profit return and guidance lift, so you may want to compare how their assumptions could shift now.
